channel.title: Crypto Bulletin
channel.description: Crypto Bulletin reports crypto news on bitcoin, ethereum, stablecoins, exchanges, DeFi protocols, regulation, security incidents and market structure.

item.title: How to Recover a Mantle Bridge Transfer After Closing the Page
item.description: Closing Mantle’s bridge page does not erase a submitted transfer. Use the original wallet and transaction hash to check progress, then finish any withdrawal claim.

item.title: Why Bridges Need Gas on Both Chains
item.description: A bridge moves tokens across networks, but each chain charges for its own transactions. Learn when ETH is needed on both sides and how to avoid a stuck transfer.

item.title: LP token burns and reserve withdrawals change different things
item.description: Burning LP tokens can remove a claim on pooled assets, while withdrawing reserves changes the pool itself; transaction details show which event occurred.

item.title: How Much Slippage Should You Set for a BNB Smart Chain Swap?
item.description: A 0.5% starting point suits many liquid BNB Smart Chain swaps, but pool depth, price movement and token fees determine when a wider limit is justified.

item.title: How to Cancel a Pending Transaction Before Bridging
item.description: A pending wallet transaction can often be replaced before it reaches the chain; after a bridge deposit or withdrawal is confirmed, the bridge’s own process takes over.

item.title: Multisignature Bridge Withdrawals Need Two Approvals
item.description: Treasury teams can approve a Polygon PoS withdrawal in two stages, with the multisig authorizing the Polygon burn and later the Ethereum claim after checkpointing.

item.title: Polygon Bridge Transfers: From Send to Arrival
item.description: A Polygon PoS bridge deposit locks tokens on Ethereum, mints a matching balance on Polygon, and completes after the source transaction is confirmed.

item.title: When Does an Omnichain Transfer Need Destination Liquidity?
item.description: A cross-chain transfer needs destination liquidity when it must pay out or swap existing assets; mint-and-release designs can settle without a local pool.

item.title: How NFT Bridges Move a Token Between Chains
item.description: An NFT bridge locks or burns the source token, sends a verified message, then releases or mints its counterpart; metadata and provenance depend on the design.

item.title: How to Retry a Stuck Destination Swap
item.description: A destination swap can fail after the bridge transfer succeeds. Check both chains, verify the received asset and gas, then retry only the failed leg.

item.title: How to Pay Gas on a New Chain With USDC
item.description: USDC does not automatically pay a new chain’s gas: check whether the network accepts stablecoin fees, then bridge funds or source its native token before transacting.

item.title: What Bridge-Wrapped Tokens Represent Across Chains
item.description: Bridge-wrapped tokens carry an asset across chains through bridge contracts; their value depends on how the bridge holds, issues and redeems the representation.

item.title: Four Checks for Keeping Wrapped XMR on the Right Chain
item.description: A wrapped XMR token works only on the network where its contract lives; check chain ID, token address, bridge record and redemption route before using it.

item.title: How to Bridge XMR Into Your Own Sepolia Wallet
item.description: ZeroFi routes real XMR to zXMR on Ethereum Sepolia; here is the wallet setup, deposit flow, confirmation wait and trade-off behind the testnet token.

item.title: How TRON Swap Routing Changes the Price You Receive
item.description: TRON swap routing can improve a quote by comparing pools, but each hop adds fees and price impact; slippage settings and execution costs also shape your final amount.

item.title: Why TRC-20 USDT swaps need TRX for network fees
item.description: A TRC-20 USDT swap runs through TRON smart contracts, which use Energy and Bandwidth; TRX covers any resource shortfall unless a wallet or service pays.

item.title: Bridge receipts show a transfer; destination balances show delivery
item.description: Bridge receipts record a cross-chain transfer, while destination balances show tokens actually delivered; check both before treating a route as complete.

item.title: Move Collateral Before a Lending Top-Up
item.description: Move collateral before a lending top-up by checking the loan’s health factor, bridging the right asset, and allowing for settlement and price changes.

item.title: Why Wallet Bridges Can Cost More Than Exchange Withdrawals
item.description: A wallet bridge can cost more because it pays for on-chain execution and cross-chain settlement, while an exchange may set a separate withdrawal price.

item.title: Check TRX and Token Balances Before a Swap
item.description: Compare the token balance, spendable TRX and quoted output before signing; the gap between wallet totals and swap costs shows what the trade will use.
